page: The Vultr vcg-l40s-16c-180g-48vram is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for high-density compute, artificial intelligence workloads, and data-intensive pipelines. The hardware configuration features 16 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6448H processor clocked at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory provisioning stands at 180 GB of system RAM, yielding a high ratio of 11.25 GB per core. The server includes dedicated hardware acceleration via a single NVIDIA L40S GPU with 48 GB of Ada Lovelace VRAM, bundled alongside 1200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional machine learning inference capabilities. The server achieves top-tier results in large language model inference, delivering 13,631.52 tokens per second for prompt processing on small (135M) models and 6,293.73 tokens per second on medium (7B) models, alongside generation speeds of 610.8 and 153.1 tokens per second respectively. Processor metrics show strong single-threaded performance with a Geekbench score of 2,130, supported by AVX-512 vector extensions and robust cryptographic hardware instruction sets. Compression and decompression tests, such as bzip3 single-threaded decompression at 15.59 GB/sec, also place the instance within the upper performance brackets.

The combination of dedicated CPU cores, substantial system memory, fast local NVMe storage, and 48 GB of GPU memory delivers high efficiency for single-GPU AI workloads. While larger multi-GPU setups or distributed training tasks fall outside its single-accelerator scope, this profile minimizes memory bottlenecks for complex models. It is particularly well matched for generative AI inference, computer vision processing, 3D rendering pipelines, and medium-scale model fine-tuning.
description: The Vultr vcg-l40s-16c-180g-48vram is a GPU-accelerated server configuration built for compute-heavy AI inference and graphics processing. Powered by 16 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6448H processor operating at 2.0 GHz, the instance integrates 180 GB of system memory, providing an expansive 11.25 GB per core. Accelerated processing is driven by a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPU equipped with 48 GB of VRAM, paired with 1200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark evaluation demonstrates top-decile throughput in prompt evaluation and text generation for small and medium language models, alongside strong single-core CPU metrics and high-speed data decompression. This hardware profile provides balanced resource allocation without severe memory constraints, making the server suitable for LLM inference serving, high-throughput image and video rendering, computer vision tasks, and accelerated analytics pipelines.
